summary.headline: GK Energy FY26 standalone revenue rose 40% to INR 1,532.54 crore, with EBITDA margin at 20.44% and PAT at INR 201 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 standalone revenue crossed INR 1,500 crore for the first time, up 40% YoY, with EBITDA of INR 313 crore (20.44% margin vs 18.64%) and PAT of INR 201 crore (up 51%). Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 418.57 crore (vs INR 352 crore YoY), EBITDA INR 85.96 crore and PAT INR 59.05 crore. Installations of 61,000+ systems in FY26 (up 34%) fell short of the 70,000-75,000 guidance, which management attributed to rainfall in Maharashtra and raw material delays in late March. Net cash stood at INR 240 crore against net debt of INR 155 crore a year earlier, while working capital days rose to about 140-150 days.

financial_highlights.value: About 140-150 days (management cited 112 days at one point; 183 days in H1 FY26)
INR 710 crore (as of 31 March plus orders received after April 2026, including INR 350 crore Magel Tyala Phase 4 order)

segments.name: Solar pumps (PM-KUSUM component B / Magel Tyala)
segments.commentary: Core business, asset-light EPC model with OEM/ODM sourcing. Maharashtra share cited at 15%+ and national share at 8-9%; management says Maharashtra will remain the main focus until Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Rooftop (PM Surya Ghar / Smart Scheme)
segments.commentary: Early-stage, with more than 5 MW installed so far. Smart Scheme (1 kW, Maharashtra) is targeted at 1 lakh households at possibly lower margins; working capital is lower for Surya Ghar (cash-and-carry) and Smart Scheme runs under a ULA model with direct government payment.

segments.name: Solar cell subsidiary (DCR cells)
segments.commentary: Wholly-owned subsidiary did INR 199 crore of business in FY26 to secure DCR cell supply; long-term contract for 875 MW for the current financial year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target: roughly double FY26 volume to 120,000-140,000 pumps, with pump revenue of INR 2,200-2,400 crore and rooftop revenue of INR 600-1,000 crore, for a total of about INR 3,000 crore plus.
Management expects to keep EBITDA margin at two digits and to try for double-digit net margin; for FY27 EBITDA a 10-15% variation was called possible, though management said it was too early to say.
Analyst's worst case discussed on the call: about INR 2,500 crore revenue and INR 250 crore PAT if PM-KUSUM 2.0 is delayed; management did not confirm this figure.
Management expects to win about INR 1,400 crore of orders by end of Q1 FY27 (INR 700 crore in hand plus INR 700 crore expected from Magel Tyala Phase 5 and Smart Scheme).
Working capital is expected to stay around 140-150 days, with a long-term aim to reduce it; inventory days are down to 21.
Management will consider providing separate EBITDA guidance for the EPC and solar cell trading businesses.
capex_capacity: Monthly installation capacity is about 15,000+ systems, built through OEM/ODM long-term agreements, with the company stating it incurs no manufacturing capex.
Company dropped solar module manufacturing plans and is sourcing modules, pumps, motors and controllers under brand-labelled supply from partners in Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, UP and Kerala.

Fixed assets rose by about INR 100 crore, mainly from a corporate office (about INR 90 crore per the analyst's question), which management said was bought in place of fixed deposits used to secure bank limits.
Company has more than 1,300 field staff and covers more than 7,500 villages; cumulative renewable installations total 617 MW.
Management has no plans to enter new states in FY27; current states are UP, Haryana, Rajasthan, MP, Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is intact and that Q4 shortfall was due to rainfall and late-March raw material disruption linked to the war that started in late February.
Competitive intensity is high in pump supply: management described solar pumps as a commodity, but EPC is less competitive and brand recall with farmers matters.
Management says GK does not bid below its required margin, and that lower unit prices are offset by volume and vendor renegotiation.
Raw material risk is managed through six-month forward price freezes and 30-50% capacity commitments with 2-3 suppliers per product.
Magel Tyala Phase 5 is under evaluation and expected to open; PM-KUSUM 2.0 timing has slipped from early April to end-June per the analyst, and management said specifications are being revised.
Management did not bid on the Karnataka tender in January, citing a need to be sure of funds and demand before entering a state.
Receivables from some large state utilities improved in H2 FY26; management expects the cycle to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 installations (about 17,000) and FY26 volumes miss the roughly 50,000 H2 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is intact and blamed raw material delays and late-March rainfall in Maharashtra; FY26 volume was 60,000+ against 70,000+ guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold given raw material price pressure and competition in tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited forward procurement contracts with price freezes for 3-6 months and volume-driven cost gains, and said it aims to keep the two-digit margin.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 targets and funding plan for the working capital needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to roughly double volumes, with about INR 3,000 crore revenue, and said it will use equity raised in October, surplus reserves, and unutilised CC and BG bank limits; it gave no cost figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the corporate office purchase a concern for an asset-light company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the office was bought with fixed deposits that had been used to secure bank limits, so the cash was moved into an asset.

qa_highlights.question: How much of PM-KUSUM 2.0 can GK capture?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put its national share at about 9% and its Maharashtra share at 15%+; it expects PM-KUSUM 2.0 volumes to be two to three times the earlier scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company disclose Q1 FY27 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a quarterly number and said it would talk only on an annual basis.

risks_watch: PM-KUSUM 2.0 timing: management said it expects volume from Q3 FY27, and an analyst cited a deferral from early April to end-June.
Working capital at about 140-150 days with a rising receivables and bank-limit need, implied by the FY27 INR 3,000 crore target.
Competitive pricing in Magel Tyala and rising tender competition, with management saying realisation is under pressure.
Raw material and geopolitical risk, with management saying a 10-15% EBITDA variation is possible.
Governance: an investor asked for more frequent investor engagement, and no post-Q3 call was held. Management said it would consider this.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on volume growth and asset-light flexibility, but evasive on specifics: it gave no Q1 FY27 numbers, no separate segment margins, no working capital cost and no PM-KUSUM timing. Management also deflected the IPO and corporate office questions.
key_quotes: Demand is not at all a question.
So, we are expecting -- rather than expecting, I would say that whole management would try to double the number what we have delivered on the revenue side.
We are happy to have 1% less profit, but we want to be very clear what we are going to earn it.

adds.what: Monthly installation capacity of about 15,000+ systems via OEM/ODM long-term agreements (no manufacturing capex; not owned capacity)

growth.why: FY27 guided to roughly double FY26 volume (120,000-140,000 pumps) and ~INR 3,000 crore+ revenue, backed by INR 710 crore order book and a targeted INR 1,400 crore of orders by end Q1 FY27, though PM-KUSUM 2.0 timing has slipped and the capacity is OEM/ODM-sourced rather than owned.
